decision: Yes: loops are ordinary versions. The ABC loop subsystem retires, and the driver's key rule becomes concrete: a plain forward edge keeps constants; an edge into a function-entry pc joins that entry's lattice-keyed version (per continuation for virtual entries); an edge into a non-entry loop header uses the generic all-location key; the budget fallback uses the same generic key. Loop headers join shared module facts (a leader with an incoming edge whose source pc >= it), replacing the C sink's private scan; the C sink's per-slot recursion widening and native's backward-edge constant weakening collapse into that one rule. The key is corrected to constants + binding locations + the continuation chain. The ABC location vocabulary is justified rather than asserted: verifier-fixed join shapes make the target layout a function of the target pc, and because the body is emitted once for many predecessors while the emitter can only address the C frame, A/B values are drained into C slots at the edge (rejected alternative: key A/B positions and read them in place). Q8 answered; Q9 opened as a narrow native version-policy gate (native currently peels one iteration by keeping constants on a forward loop-header edge); Q1's case now includes the measured local-loop coverage cliff; ARCHITECTURE.md, LOG.md and QUESTIONS.md updated.

decision: The lattice is a module-level fixpoint over residual functions whose widening discards and rebuilds the entire function buffer — and it should not be built. ARCHITECTURE now makes a key exact and never widened; the only forced-generic triggers are (i) a residual-call entry, because a call that can only name a function entry must be correct for every caller, and (ii) the per-pc version budget. A residual function has exactly one generic-key entry version; there is no join, no call facts, no re-execution, no rebuild, and the module-wide invariant "each version body is executed exactly once" is restored. Specialization across calls comes from inlining: a direct call becomes a virtual entry — an ordinary version carrying the caller's constants and its continuation chain — bounded by a new per-residual-function version budget, with a residual call (generic entry) as the fallback; nontail recursive cycles must stay residual because inlining grows the continuation chain that is part of key identity. The ABC argument-fact machinery (ArgumentFact, record_call facts, activate/join_call_facts, the dirty loop), the dead residual_analysis lattice and the builder's argument_facts hook join the retired-path list, and the documented docs/abc-opt.md:25,100 behavior removal rides on Q1's gate. Q7 is revised to this answer; Q10 (ABC inline rule and its bound) and Q11 (loop-header key form: generic vs per-slot join vs exact-key unrolling) are opened; Q9's uniform-generic recommendation is weakened by the measured invariant-constant loss; Q1/Q4/Q5 are refined. The lattice alternative stays on record with its measured mechanism and cost as the fallback if cross-call constants are required.
next: Q11 is now the last place where a key is deliberately generalized while constants are still available: deciding whether "no widening anywhere except the forced entry plus the budget" is the whole key rule requires knowing the version count and code size of exact-key loop headers (a constant-initialized changing slot unrolls up to the per-pc budget and then converges to the generic version) versus one body with a loop-granular widening join. That needs a versioned-driver prototype over the optimizer corpus after Q10 fixes the ABC inline rule and its budget, and Q2 still blocks a single budget number.

(Ranked above the per-version drain/entry-layout contract, fixed by round 3's fixtures, and above where per-pc layouts/may-write sets live, opened as Q12.)
evidence: experiments/5-loop-key.md §1 and experiments/5-loop-key.lua: the incumbent's optimized documented counter (frontend/tests/optimize.lua:229) is ONE loop body at pc 6 — `CGET0_A; BLTUI_A 50` with body `CGET0_A; ADDI_A 7; ZX32_A; CGET1_A; ADDI_A 1; ZX32_A; CSETN_A 1; CSET0_A; JMP 6` — both loop-carried slots unknown while bound 50 and step 7 stay constants in the same body, and frontend/tests/optimize.lua:502,505 pins those immediates. So the documented loop header is a join that widens written slots and keeps unwritten constants.

experiments/5-loop-key.md §2 (measured, artifacts experiments/5-loop-key-out/, all return 1071 in interpreted/threaded/compiled/lazy): loop-invariant-key emission P = 16 instructions, one body, 10 instructions/iteration, `BLTUI_A 120` + `ADDI_A 7`; generic-key emission G = 22 instructions, 12/iteration, bound/step are `CGETN_B` reads; exact-key emission E with budget 8 = 29 instructions (seven folded header versions that are single jumps, four constant stores at the budget edge, then an all-location tail at 12/iteration with no immediates). Computed executed-instruction counts at trip 18: 188 / 229 / 152; exact keys win only for small constant trip counts (break-even about 36 iterations).

experiments/5-loop-key-out/G-generic.c and src/residual_builder.c:1090-1091, 1195-1207: the shipped portable-C sink materializes the bound before the loop but its loop-entry version compares block-argument copies `if(v_8 < v_5)` because `edge_version_mode` forgets constants at a loop entry; src/residualize.c:414-438 weakens all constants on a native backward edge, giving two header versions and reading an invariant C-frame bound.

Derivation (§3): a key component can differ between iterations only if the loop changes or destroys its storage, so the join's fixpoint is the entry key with the may-write components widened; that set is static (ABC: loop-interval CSET/CPUSH writes, minimum A/B/C heights, call argument bases; native: the same over A/B depths and C-frame homes), so the loop-invariant key is available when the version is created — no fixpoint, no re-execution, no rebuild, no call facts, and one version per single-entry loop header.

Consequences: a self-tail call inlines as a loop header whose backedge canonicalizes to the loop-invariant key (one-version cycle), which derives the incumbent's self-recursive inline rule (optimize.c:301,309-318) and leaves Q10's inline budget to bound only nontail chains (continuation chains in key identity, src/symbolic.c:39-75).
decision: Q11 is answered: a non-entry loop header's key is the static loop-invariant key, applied as a canonicalization to every edge into the header (every component whose storage the loop may write or destroy becomes the binding's location form; every other component keeps its constant). Exact keys at a loop header are rejected for ABC/native (the budget fallback moves the hot body to the all-location key, losing the documented `BLTUI_A 50`/`ADDI_A 7` and emitting up to `budget` bodies for a win that ends around trip 36); the round-3 generic key is rejected (measured 2 extra instructions per iteration and no immediates); the dynamic join stays rejected because the static may-write pre-widening subsumes it without a fixpoint or rebuild. ARCHITECTURE now has three static canonicalization points (residual-call/module entry → all-location; non-entry loop header → loop-invariant; per-pc budget → all-location), a loop may-write fact in module facts, a "one version per loop header" invariant, per-version (not per-pc) layout wording, and three rejected alternatives with their measured costs. Q9 is revised to a native version-policy gate with the recommendation to adopt (one header version instead of two, invariant C-frame constants kept, the peel dropped); Q12 opens where per-pc layouts and may-write sets are computed; Q4/Q5/Q10/Q1 refined. Deliverables are committed as `arch_loop round 5`.

question: Round 5 fixed the loop-header key form (loop-invariant) but sketched the load-bearing may-write predicate concretely as a pc interval [header..largest backedge source] plus a CALL/TCALL argument clause. What exactly is "the loop body", and is the backedge instruction — especially a self-tail call that rebuilds the frame — part of the body or the join? (Ranked above whether may-write is a correctness condition, answered as a by-product, and above Q12's fact ownership, refined.)
evidence: experiments/6-may-write.md §2 and experiments/6-may-write.lua (artifacts 6-may-write-out/counter.dis, exit-pop.dis): on the exact documented counter (frontend/tests/optimize.lua:229), `loop` is function 2, header pc 0x29, C height 4, one self-tail `TCALL` backedge at pc 0x48, body CSETs slots 2 and 3. Round 5's interval+CALL/TCALL rule marks may-write {0,1,2,3} (0 of 4 constants kept — the generic G key), because the tail call replaces the frame and gathers arguments at C base 4-4=0; the cycle-body rule marks {2,3} (2 of 4 constants kept), which is the incumbent's measured two-unknown-slot body with `BLTUI_A 50`/`ADDI_A 7`. So round 5's own predicate makes its flagship P shape unreachable.

experiments/6-may-write.md §3: an exit-path fixture whose exit pops the frame (CGET.A 0; CPOP; CPOP; CPOP; RET) is marked {0,1,2} by the pc interval (min C height 0) and {0} by the cycle body (min C height 3). The interval contains live code that is not on a cycle through the header, so round 5's 'dead code in the interval only over-widens' is false.

experiments/6-may-write.md §4–6: exact keys are the correctness rule, so may-write is a heuristic — over-widening loses constants, under-widening only makes the backedge create another version (bounded by the per-pc budget, Q2), and every version body stays correct. The call clause is unnecessary: a callee frame starts at the caller's call-time C height (src/symbolic.c:467-484), a callee addresses only its own C frame (src/verify.c C cases), machine_return restores frame.cbase, and a residualized call does not change n[C]; caller-side pops are already caught by the min-height clause. The ABC A/B clause is vacuous because ABC keys are A/B-empty after round 3's drain.

experiments/6-gather.lua and experiments/6-gather3.lua (all four execution modes): the ABC gather is slot-identity — argument 0 is the first pushed value, callee C_k <- selected-stack depth k (`f(1,2,3)` returns `1 2 3` from CGET 0,1,2), matching docs/spec.md 'Calls' and gen/banked.lua:234. A same-function self-tail transport therefore preserves positions; a computed/re-ordered argument vector is widened at the edge (quality, not soundness).

experiments/6-may-write.md §7: a cross-function tail cycle (mutual tail calls) has no per-function cycle body and no position identity, so round 5's claim that mutual tail recursion keeps its invariant constants is unsupported — the conservative answer is the all-location key or no inlining (Q14).
decision: Q13 is answered: the loop body is the cycle body (pcs on a path from the header to a backedge source, excluding the backedge instructions), and the backedge instruction is the join, not a body write — a self-tail TCALL defines the target frame from its argument vector exactly as binding.join defines a join target. The ABC predicate is C-only: slot k is may-write iff the cycle body's min C height <= k or a CSET in the cycle body targets k; native adds A/B depth d iff min A/B height <= d. The pc interval and the CALL/TCALL clause are rejected with measured costs (interval+CALL: 0 constants kept on the documented counter; cycle body: 2 — the incumbent's shape; exit-pop: {0,1,2} vs {0}). May-write is stated as a specialization heuristic, not a correctness condition: exact keys keep any widening sound, under-widening only adds versions bounded by the per-pc budget, so no fixpoint, no completeness obligation and no cross-function analysis is needed. ARCHITECTURE now names the cycle body/backedge-as-join/transport and the heuristic status, records the rejected interval predicate with its numbers, adds backedge instructions/cycle bodies/per-pc heights/CSET targets to module facts, pins Q12's data set, and opens Q14 (cross-function tail cycles, where round 5's invariant-constant claim does not hold). Q5/Q10/Q11/Q12 are refined; deliverables committed as `arch_loop round 6`.
next: Q14 (do cross-function tail cycles keep invariants, or take the all-location key / stay residual), then Q12's ownership decision: one shared shape/cycle-body pass in the core, with the verifier's discarded Shape heights showing the data is already computed today. Q2 still blocks a single budget number and Q1 remains the scope gate.

question: Does the per-pc version budget bound all version multiplicity, or only versions inside one continuation chain? A key is constants + locations + the continuation chain, and the design claimed the budget's all-location fallback is a canonicalization like the entry/loop rules. If no widening can remove a chain, what bounds the number of inlined call instances (families) at a pc, and with what fallback? Ranked above (B) the key of a version that is both an inlined callee entry and a cycle header (answered as a corollary: the entry key is the call ABI, not an edge canonicalization) and (C) Q14 (unaffected: tail calls push no continuation).
evidence: experiments/7-budget.md §1-§4: key equality compares the continuation chain (src/symbolic.c:45-53) and family equality adds the stack shape (:56-66), while every canonicalization in every sink is value-only (src/residual_builder.c:851-868, 936-963). So the all-location fallback is total *inside* a family and cannot merge two call instances: versions(pc) = families(pc) x budget. The only code that removes a chain is a call decision (src/residualize.c:395-406). This is the gap REFACTOR.md:811 recorded ('family count includes the continuation chain ... 10 versions at one entry PC' vs the approved eight-total wording).

experiments/7-budget.md §2: a call continuation records return pc, target and the call-time bases (src/symbolic.c:471-477); the verifier fixes the shape at each pc (src/verify.c:284), so the chain is the call path: #families(pc) = #inlined non-tail call instances. Tail calls push no continuation (src/symbolic.c:486-499), so self-tail backedges keep one chain (why the loop key is stable) and multiplicity comes only from non-tail inlining, which docs/abc-opt.md:82-91 requires.

experiments/7-call-paths.py and measurements in experiments/7-budget.md §3: a branch-free doubling call ladder f_i(x)=f_{i+1}(x)+f_{i+1}(x| x+1) has 2^depth syntactic call instances; the ABC sink's output doubles with the instance count (22, 46, 94, 190, 382, 766 instructions for 8..256 instances, ~1.75-3 per instance), independent of branches, until ABC's 255-cell C-frame limit stops outer inlining at depth 9 (src/optimize.c:753, 762). A versioned sink emits one body per inlined instance because the chain differs, so this is the multiplicity its budget must cut; the per-pc key budget cannot.

experiments/6-may-write-out/counter.dis: the documented counter's loop header pc 0x29 *is* function 2's entry and the self-tail TCALL returns to 0x29. A pc-scoped residual-call-entry canonicalization (the current 'non-entry loop header' wording) would apply the all-location key there and make round 6's measured P shape (may-write {2,3}, BLTUI_A 50/ADDI_A 7) unreachable. The entry generic key belongs to the callee's own residual-function entry (the call ABI), not to the edge.

src/residualize.c:395-406, 408-414, 424-437 and src/residual_builder.c:1108-1117 confirm the three existing behaviours: native stops inlining at the target-pc continuation limit, fails the compile at the family limit without a generic context, and the C sink falls back to the all-location form inside a family. None bounds families.

QUESTIONS.md Q15 (answered), Q2 (refined from a number to number *and scope*: per-family vs total-per-pc), Q10 (bound sharpened to the driver's continuation-family count with a residual-call fallback), Q11 (word 'non-entry' retired); ARCHITECTURE.md now states two key rules (entry = call ABI; every edge into a loop header = loop-invariant key), a per-family budget with the all-location 'general slot', and a separate inlining bound K with a residual-call fallback: families(pc) <= K, versions(pc) <= K*budget, work bounded by sum_functions (1+K)*code(f)*budget. Rejected/recorded alternatives: chain widening, a literal total-per-pc budget, a pc-scoped entry rule, a static capped call-path fact, and a per-function-only budget.
decision: The per-pc budget is not a canonicalization of the version key; it is a **per-family** budget (family = stack shape + continuation chain), because no value widening can change a chain and the chain names an inlined call's return site. The design now has two key rules — a residual function's entry version is the generic all-location key because that is the call ABI (the caller materializes arguments into binding locations), and every edge into a loop header takes the loop-invariant key, including an inlined callee entry that is a cycle header — plus two bounds: the per-family budget (all-location fallback, total inside the family) and a separate inlining bound K on distinct continuation families per target pc (fallback: residual call, the only operation that drops a chain). Invariants: families(pc) <= K, versions(pc) <= K x budget. This also fixes the flagship P shape under a literal reading (the documented counter's loop header is the inlined callee's function entry), retires the pc-scoped entry rule and the pc-scoped entry language, and turns Q2 from a number question into a number-and-scope hard gate (a literal "eight total per pc" is unenforceable by key widening). Measured multiplicity: a branch-free doubling call ladder emits 22/46/94/190/382/766 instructions for 8..256 inlined instances (~1.75-3 per instance) until ABC's 255-cell frame limit; the per-pc key budget cannot reduce any of it. Committed as `arch_loop round 7`.
next: Q2's scope decision is now the last hard gate for a single budget owner: if the user requires a total-versions-per-pc cap, a shared budget between constant families and continuation chains must be designed before the driver is buildable; otherwise the per-family 8 plus K is the coherent policy. After that: Q12's fact ownership (one shared shape/cycle-body pass in the core), then Q10's K value / static-vs-dynamic inlining bound and Q14 (unchanged; tail cycles create one chain). Not established: corpus chain multiplicities, the right K, and whether the versioned ABC sink's loss of cross-instance value CSE is material.

question: Is a version key's identity its value content (constants, binding locations, frame coordinates, continuation chain), or also the canonicalisation mode — and does version creation look the key up after the budget widens it? The round-7 algorithm looked up the incoming key only, then created the all-location key, and the incumbent's `abc_symbolic_context_equal` compares a stored `generic` bit that `canonicalize` sets from the widening argument.
evidence: experiments/8-version-model.py and 8-version-model.out: abstract key space (one family, 2 components, all 9 arrival vectors, BFS over reachable version tables, budget 3). Lookup-before-widening reaches 4/6/8/10 versions for arrival sequences of length 4/6/8/10 — unbounded, with duplicate all-location keys; content identity + lookup-after-widening saturates at 3 = budget with one version per value vector. The loop-header-entry configuration is 2 versions (both with the same value vector) with the mode bit, 1 version / 0 duplicates with content identity.

src/symbolic.c:51-72,74-85: exact equality compares `c_origin`, `c_bias`, the stored `generic` bit, the chain and the values; `canonical_generic_context` recomputes the same property from the values; family equality ignores the bit and the limits. src/residual_builder.c:851-866,1088-1121: `canonicalize` sets `generic = forget_constants`; `VERSION_LOOP_ENTRY` is literally `canonicalize(key,1)` (why the C sink's loop entry forgets invariants); the budget path widens then calls `find_version` again. src/residualize.c:161-169,408-438: `conform_generic` sets the bit and zeroes limits; `version_for` checks `generic_context_equal` first; an exact match additionally requires `in->limit >= v->in.limit` (proven headroom, a split-only binding refinement).

Consequence in the design: a residual entry supplies only locations and may-write widening can only remove constants, so the all-location entry key and a loop-invariant backedge key at a loop-header entry PC have the same value vector — with the mode bit they are two versions/two bodies in one family (the round-7 text's 'one body per loop header per family' and 'entry has exactly one version' both violated); with content identity they are one version, i.e. the entry version is the loop-header version, so the `create(f.entry, …)` bypass is unnecessary.

Q14 evidence sharpened in passing: `nested_eligible = recursive && call-component size == 1 && !nontail` (src/optimize.c:108-114), and `dag_tail`/`dag_call` inline only via `nested_eligible` or a self-tail to the root (src/optimize.c:299-318) — the incumbent residualizes every mutual call, tail or not, so the design's cross-function-tail-cycle claim has no canonical-output support.

ARCHITECTURE.md updated (key/family definitions, invariants, data representation, algorithm block, bounds, interfaces, evidence); two new rejected alternatives with the model numbers; Q16 added and answered in QUESTIONS.md; LOG.md round-8 section appended; committed as 27cc8b2 `arch_loop round 8`.
decision: Key identity is content: constants, the binding's location at each position, the frame coordinates and the continuation chain; how a key was canonicalised is never part of it ("all-location/generic" is a derived predicate, so a unique value key per family). `version_at` looks every key up after every widening, including the budget fallback, so the general slot exists at most once and a family holds at most budget-1 exact keys plus one general slot; this restores the headline bound `versions(pc) <= families(pc) x budget` and the one-body-per-key invariant that the round-7 algorithm violated. The residual-function entry is created through `version_at` with the all-location value key — the loop rule is a fixed point on it, so an entry pc that is a loop header has one body, not two. A binding may add a resource condition that only splits a core key (native proven headroom); a split stays inside one family and is counted by the same budget. The stored `generic` mode bit in equality and the lookup-before-widening order are recorded as rejected alternatives with the model numbers. Q2/Q12 unchanged; the per-family budget and Q15's answer stand.
next: Q14's policy is now the only remaining key-rule question with a concept cost: inline a cross-function mutual tail cycle (needs a module-wide cycle body with tail-call edges, or accepts exact keys at the header up to the budget) or residualize it as the incumbent's `nested_eligible` does — then Q2's scope decision (per-family vs total-per-pc), Q12's one-owner fact pass, and Q10's K value. Also unmeasured: whether any real module reaches the loop-header-entry configuration other than a hand-built two-root case, and whether the family scan (linear in versions at a pc) is acceptable compile cost.

question: A canonical in-repo fixture (frontend/tests/compiler.lua:790-804, docs/abc-opt.md:100) pins residual-entry invariant specialization for a mutual tail-recursive SCC, while the design's residual entry is the generic all-location key (Q7). Is that documented precision recoverable by any key rule, and what does the design's inline rule for cross-function tail cycles (Q14) have to say? Ranked above Q2's total-vs-per-family scope (whose design-side answer is a corollary: a new family at a pc arrives only on a call edge, so a one-pass driver can only bound value keys inside a family) and Q12's fact ownership.
evidence: experiments/9-tail-cycle.md, experiments/9-tail-cycle.lua, experiments/9-tail-cycle.out, artifacts in experiments/9-tail-cycle-out/.

frontend/tests/compiler.lua:790-804 is live (Makefile:212; suite passes) and stages mutual even/odd with default optimize=true, so it asserts abc-opt output: 3 functions, TCALL, PUSH8_A 9, PUSH8_A 10; docs/abc-opt.md:100 documents the same behavior.

Measured: pre-optimizer 48 instructions reads the parameter (CGETN_A 4/3) and adds; abc-opt 21 instructions folds marker to PUSH8_A 9 in even and marker+1 to PUSH8_A 10 in odd, value 9 in off/threaded/eager/lazy, opt a byte-identical fixpoint (src/optimize.c:850-873 is the mechanism).

Measured oracle: even(4,9)+even(4,7) (value 16, all four modes) widens marker, and the callee bodies become the generic-entry shape - even 9 instructions unchanged, odd 9 -> 11 (CGET1_A; ADDI_A 1; ZX32_A instead of PUSH8_A 10). That +2 is the design's cost; module 21 -> 23.
docs/spec.md:167-170: CALL gathers argument zero at C0 and the callee has empty private A/B stacks, so the ABC residual entry IS the all-location form (no entry prologue, no separate question).
src/optimize.c:108-114,299-318: nested_eligible = recursive && call-component size 1 && !nontail; dag_tail/dag_call inline only via it or a self-tail to the root - the derived form of the kept rule.
decision: Q14 answered: every cross-function recursive call, tail or not, is a residual call; the only inlined recursion is a same-function self-tail cycle (callee == caller, component size 1, no nontail call) which is a loop header under the loop rule. No module-wide cycle body, no cross-function transport fact. Reason: a residual call's entry is the all-location key, so no constant can cross and the loop rule (which only preserves constants already in a key) is a no-op on it; inlining the SCC is the only way to carry its constants but changes the documented three-function/TCALL shape, duplicates the cycle per call site, and still cannot keep invariants in the hot body without a module-wide cycle body. The design therefore states as a rule, not a sink limitation: only inlined recursion keeps constants; a residual recursive function (mutual or self-tail) has a no-op loop rule. The measured price is the canonical fixture's odd body 9 -> 11 instructions and the two compiler.lua:803 immediate assertions, which join docs/abc-opt.md:100 under Q1/Q7's already-raised output gate.
